## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vighāsādajātaka* (Ja 393) is a canonical Jātaka tale belonging to the late Khuddaka Nikāya collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the tale while residing at the East Garden (*Pubbārāma*) in reference to a group of monks who had become given to frivolity and amusement [SuttaCentral]. After the Elder Mahāmoggallāna shook their dwelling to alarm and sober them, the monks gathered in the Dhamma Hall to discuss their shortcoming, whereupon the Buddha revealed that they had displayed the same frivolous tendencies in a previous birth [SuttaCentral].

Verses from the text address the ethical definition of an "eater of leftovers" (*vighāsāda* / *vighāsādin*) [Fausböll 1883]. While ascetics (*tāpasā*) living on the scraps left behind by predatory beasts such as lions and tigers (*vāḷānañ câvasiṭṭhakaṁ*) consider themselves *vighāsādino*, the verse dialogue clarifies that true eaters of leftovers are those who first offer food to a brahmin, an ascetic, or any other mendicant (*vanibbi*), and only partake of whatever remains [Fausböll 1883].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify thematic or verse resemblances with chapter 5 (*Priyavarga*) of the *Udānavarga*, its Tibetan (*Uv Kg* 5) and Sanskrit (*UVS* 5) versions, the Chinese translations T 212.6 and T 213.5, as well as the *Tittirajātaka* (Ja 37) and the Vinaya *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers ten passages of Pali-internal text reuse with the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (matching up to 803 characters, §3.4–4.5), reflecting the embedded canonical verses and commentary, while detecting no automated cross-language parallels meeting its score threshold [DharmaNexus].
